decisions.text: type heatmap: 32 series, more than a stack of small charts holds (about 20–30): a heatmap, a row per series (G1.20, G7.35; D-28)
the title wraps onto two lines
no values in the cells; the values do not fit their cells: the colour alone, read against the key (G5.13)
the cells strong: a heatmap, whose colour is the message: the steps at full strength (owner, 1 Oct 2026)
the cells: a diverging palette; the audience sees a dividing value, 0: two ramps meeting at a neutral there (G4.11, G4.12)
the cells: the sides are not judged good or bad (no measure.good): blue below 0, orange above, the pair safe for colour-vision deficiency and free of red (G4.17, G4.18)
the cells: the distances from 0 are fairly even (the fullest of seven equal steps would hold 27 % of them): equal steps on rounded values, the most honest cut

a key: a bar of the 7 classes, “Temperature against the 1961–1990 average (°C)” above it, −3, −2, −1, 0, +1, +2, +3 under it, a tick at the dividing value, and a separate entry for the 8 values not known, above the grid at its right (G5.13, s. 0204)
the lightest step #ddeef8: OKLab ΔE 0.065 from the page and 0.215 from the missing grey; the breaks in the key rounded and formatted as a set
the cells coloured in classes, diverging about 0, equal steps of the distance from it, 3 classes a side, at +1, +2, +3, darker meaning further from the dividing value on each side (G4.12, G4.14)
8 values not known in grey cells, never the colour of zero (G7.35)
time axis: every 5th year, on the years divisible by 5 (round years, which the eye counts on; every label would crowd)

source.notes: 03-04 #8, #9 (diverging about the audience's dividing value); 06 T14
source.shows: a heatmap of many series over time whose colour diverges about a value the audience sees as dividing, the stations' own long-term average (0 °C), with no good or bad side (no measure.good): blue below and orange above, the colour-blind-safe ramp, free of red (G4.11, G4.17); symmetric about 0 and keyed by a graduated bar with a tick at 0; a few years not recorded, grey; synthetic data in the shape of the UK record (a warming trend, cold 1986 and 2010, warm 2014 and 2022); variant sequential, the same values on one ramp (a guided departure, reported), where the cold years no longer read as cold; variant diverging-about-the-middle, a diverging ramp asked for without a dividing value, refused (R3-13)
